messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: label switching in mixture models
parts:
Hi,

Can someone advise how to deal with label switching in the finite mixture model?  Attached is the model and trace for 2 and 20 component mixture (ending in .2.pdf and .20.pdf correspondingly).  Looks like that parameters that are directly related to mixture components (theta, loc_phi, scale_phi) don't mix well - perhaps because of label switching - while mixing for other parameters is decent.

Thanks for any insight,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] label switching in mixture models
parts:
If your inferences don't depend on labels,
you can calculate the inferences directly and
measure their convergence properties.

Sometimes the mixture components can be identified,
as by an ordering constraint or a strong enough prior.

Otherwise, you have to try to put them back
together after the fact, which is painful.

- Bob

> On May 2, 2015, at 3:15 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks, Bob. Is it possible to expand on option 2 and 3?
>
> In option 2 we have to impose ordering constraints on mixture parameter simplex [K] theta - what is a good way?

There's no good way to do this directly. You can use
an ordered vector and softmax it to get an ordered simplex.
> In option 3 we have to go through all draws and flip the draw from theta[draw,1] to theta[draw,2] if ordering constraint is violated. Right?

Yes, or come up with some other way of reassociating the
parameter values.

And yes, it looks like theta[1] and theta[2] are getting reversed.

- Bob
